title: Surgeon Rollout: Coordinated version rewind and tenant triage procedures for asymmetric canary regressions
creator: Asha Raman
description: Summary: Create and validate an operational playbook and tooling to perform a minimal-impact

’surgeon rollback’ — a rapid, tenant-aware version rewind for models that degrade in quality or latency in asymmetric canaries across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The focus is safe, repeatable remediation that preserves tenant isolation, handles KV-cache desynchronization, and provides clear customer communication and follow-through.

Motivation: Recent incidents revealed gaps in our ability to surgically reverse model rollouts that affect only a subset of tenants or slices. Current blunt rollbacks either impact unaffected tenants or leave degraded slices exposed while we build fixes. This ticket captures the runbook, automation checklist, and customer liaison templates to minimize MTTA/MTTR and reduce customer escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Validated playbook that operators can execute within 15 minutes for common regression patterns
Automation scripts to pin and rollback model versions per-tenant in Hosted and Dedicated within existing RBAC constraints
KV-cache reconciliation checklist documented and integrated with deployment tooling
Customer communication templates (initial, interim, resolution) reviewed by PM and Support
POST-INCIDENT action items created automatically in tracking system after any surgeon rollback event
reproduction_steps: Trigger: detect a quality or latency regression via model-quality monitors or SLO alerts on canary slice
1) Identify affected slice: query canary-slicer dashboard for feature gates and tenant IDs
2) Confirm regression: run golden prompt set against canary and baseline model versions via eval infra
3) Verify isolation: confirm traffic routing for the slice (split-key, route rules) and model variant mapping
4) Simulate rewind in staging with identical route rules and KV cache seed to validate cache reconciliation steps
mitigation_steps: Immediate: engage on-call and designate incident operator and customer liaison
Cut traffic: if regression is high-severity, use traffic control API to divert slice traffic to baseline model variant for affected tenants only
Surgeon rollback (per-tenant): use automated pin tool to set model.version=prior for tenant slice; ensure placement respects Dedicated pool quotas
KV-cache handling: run kvcache-invalidate for the tenant's nodes and optionally prewarm KV cache by replaying recent requests in a staging replica
Throttling: enable token-level soft-throttle for degraded model variant to stabilize latencies while rollback completes
Smoke tests: run end-to-end smoke tests (latency + quality) on affected slice before returning to normal ramp-down of diversion
operator_checklist: Confirm customer(s) impacted list and priority
Open incident channel and attach runbook link
Run golden prompt set and attach outputs to the incident
Execute per-tenant pin via rollout-api and confirm via config service
Execute kvcache reconciliation steps (invalidate -> prewarm) and monitor cache hit/miss metrics
Monitor traces and latency histograms for immediate regressions
Notify Support and PM using templated messages
If rollback fails, escalate to runtime-oncall and SRE
automation_notes: - per-tenant atomic setModelVersion(tenant, model, version) with idempotency token
- dry-run mode that simulates KV cache changes and reports expected nodes affected
dashboard: add 'surgeon rollback' quick action and one-click incident annotation
communication_templates: Initial customer note: 'We're investigating a model regression affecting your tenant. We've routed your traffic to a stable variant; we'll update you within 30 minutes with next steps.'
Interim update: 'Root cause analysis in progress. We have performed an isolated rollback for your tenant and are monitoring for improvements. Expect a detailed postmortem within 72 hours.'

Resolution: 'The regression has been resolved by rolling back to the prior model version for your tenant. We will follow up with remediation and timeline to reintroduce new model versions once tested.'
review_feedback: PM (Riley Chen): please add exact SLAs for notification windows and confirm Support escalation thresholds
Design (Nora Patel): add templated console banners for affected tenant pages and include visible rollback audit trail
SRE (Jordan Li): ensure kvcache invalidation has circuit breakers to avoid mass invalidation across Dedicated hosts
Security (Priya Shah): confirm rollback API requires two-person approval when acting on Private/VPC tenants
postmortem_tasks: Capture timeline and decision points into incident report
Root cause analysis of why the canary diverged (model, data, serving path)
Automate golden prompt smoke runs as pre-merge gating for rollout pipeline
Add telemetry to detect asymmetric regressions earlier (per-tenant quality deltas)
Schedule tabletop exercise with Support, PM, and SRE to practice surgeon rollback flow
notes: Design principle: prefer targeted tenant-level rewinds over global rollbacks where possible
Be mindful of data residency for Private deployments—approval may be required before acting
Always document KV-cache actions in the rollback audit trail to help reconcile later inconsistencies
